title: Consumption testing harness and synthetic-playbook PRD
author: Asha Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose: This PRD defines the "consumption testing harness" and accompanying synthetic-traffic playbook used by Product, SRE, and Applied ML to validate economics, SLOs, and fidelity regressions before rolling model or runtime changes to customers. The harness standardizes load generation, telemetry collection, and cost/inference quality assertions so releases are validated against realistic, repeatable consumption scenarios.

Scope

- Included: hosted and dedicated serving modes, streaming and non-streaming endpoints, model variants (base/quantized/adapter), prefix/KV-cache retention behavior, and Cost/SLO regressions for per-route contracts.
- Excluded: on-prem private deployments (handled by eng-private-deployments runbooks), upstream model weighting experiments (handled by Applied ML lab).

Goals

1. Provide an automated harness ("consumption-sim") that can run scenario suites representing 6 canonical workload archetypes (interactive chat, transactional completion, embedding bulk indexing, concurrent short-chat bursts, long-context summarization, reranking). Each scenario must be parameterizable for concurrency, request distribution, and token length histograms.
2. Produce deterministic telemetry artifacts for each run: token counts, latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), per-token egress cost estimate, model output fidelity delta (against golden prompts), cache hit/miss rates.
3. Include a standardized set of regression checks and alerting rules that gate canary rollouts.
4. Support developer-level local runs (developer runtime sandbox) and CI-level runs that integrate with Redwood CI and the Release Orchestrator.

Non-goals

- This PRD does not prescribe pricing changes or billing pipeline changes. It only produces signals that product/finance can use.
- It does not attempt to simulate complex customer data leakage patterns or PII-sensitive workloads.

Requirements (Functional and Measurable)

1) Scenario definitions (must):
   - S1: Interactive-chat (90/10 prompt/response ratio) with median request size 40 tokens, median response 120 tokens.
   - S2: Transactional-completion (idempotent short responses) median request 12 tokens, response 16 tokens.
   - S3: Embeddings-bulk (batch 1k items) payloads of 128 tokens, throughput target 2k embeddings/min.
   - S4: Burst-short-chat (sudden spikes to 2x baseline concurrency for 2 minutes).
   - S5: Long-context (2k-token prefix + generation up to 1k tokens).
   - S6: Reranking (N=50 candidates, model scoring only).

2) Telemetry outputs (must):
   - JSON artifact per experiment with fields: scenario_id, run_id, start_ts, end_ts, per-route token_count, latency_histogram (buckets), model_variant, kv_cache_hit_ratio, estimated_cost_usd. The harness must export these to redwood-telemetry S3 staging for downstream analysis.

3) Regression checks (must):
   - Latency: p95 increase <= 12% relative to baseline run for same scenario and model variant.
   - Cost: per-token egress cost delta <= 10% when switching kernels or quantization profile.
   - Fidelity: for golden prompt set, BLEU-like (or embed-sim) drop <= 0.025 average delta for completions and embed-sim >= 0.98 for embeddings.
   - Cache: kv_cache_hit_ratio change <= 5 percentage points.

4) Automation and CI integration (must):
   - A job template for Redwood CI that can be parameterized with scenario, model-variant, and capacity-shape.
   - A webhook that triggers canary gating: when regression checks fail, Release Orchestrator must block canary promotion and create a ticket in the Release Tracking board.

5) Developer ergonomics (must):
   - Local sandbox CLI: consumption-sim run --scenario S1 --duration 10m --concurrency 8 --collect telemetry.json
   - Docker-compose / local-runtime profile that can simulate a small-scale dedicated pool and local telemetry sink.

Architecture and components

- consumption-sim: Core harness service (python/async) that orchestrates request generators, collects traces, and emits artifacts. It runs test suites and supports pluggable workload drivers (http/gRPC/stream).
- workload-drivers: Modules for chat, embeddings (bulk), reranking, and long-context generation.
- telemetry-exporter: Writes standardized artifacts to S3 under s3://redwood-test-artifacts/{run_id}/ and emits aggregates to redwood-telemetry via push API.
- comparison-service: Lightweight comparator that computes fidelity deltas against golden sets using embedding-sim and token-diff heuristics.
- ci-job-template: YAML used by Redwood CI + Release Orchestrator to schedule runs and evaluate gating rules.

Synthetic traffic profile matrix (example)

| Scenario | Concurrency | Avg req tokens | Avg resp tokens | 90th percentile seq_len | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| S1 interactive-chat | 16 | 40 | 120 | 350 | mimic customer-facing chat app (mixed warm/cold sessions) |
| S2 transactional | 200 | 12 | 16 | 24 | high-concurrency low-latency endpoints |
| S3 embeddings-bulk | 8 (batch=1k) | 128 | N/A | 128 | bulk ingestion pattern, high GPU throughput |
| S4 burst-short-chat | baseline*2 for 120s | 20 | 60 | 100 | scheduled spike to test autoscale policies |
| S5 long-context | 4 | 2000 | 800 | 2800 | tests KV cache pressure and kernel selection overlaps |
| S6 reranking | 32 | N/A | N/A (score only) | N/A | large candidate sets for scorer-only runs |
Runbook: How to execute a typical validation run

1) Prepare baseline artifacts: pull latest baseline artifact for scenario from s3://redwood-test-artifacts/baselines/{scenario}/latest.json.
2) Provision environment: select target mode (hosted/dedicated) and model-variant. For dedicated, use the staging pool name "staging-dedicated-1".
3) Start run: consumption-sim run --scenario S1 --model gptx-base-8bit --duration 30m --concurrency 16 --export s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/{run_id}/telemetry.json
4) Monitor: watch redwood-telemetry dashboard (Consumption Test suite) for in-flight metrics: token_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, cache_hit_ratio.
5) Post-process: comparison-service compare --baseline s3://redwood-test-artifacts/baselines/S1/latest.json --candidate s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/{run_id}/telemetry.json --out s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/{run_id}/comparison.json
6) Gate check: run gating-rule-evaluator --artifact s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/{run_id}/comparison.json. If any check fails, the CLI returns non-zero and the Release Orchestrator webhook must block canary promotion.

Acceptance criteria for feature completion

- The harness must be able to run all 6 canonical scenarios on both hosted and a small dedicated staging pool with documented commands.
- The produced telemetry JSON schema must pass the telemetry-schema linter (telemetry-schema v1.2).
- The gating rules (latency, cost, fidelity thresholds above) are implemented and documented in CI templates.
- At least three feature teams (Serving Runtime, Optimize, and Console) have run the harness in their release QA and sign-off.

Operational and implementation notes

- Telemetry retention: experiment artifacts are kept 90 days in the test-artifacts S3 bucket by default. Long-term baselines are snapshot-managed monthly.
- Cost estimation: use local unit-cost table stored at artifacts/cost-table.yaml with CPU/GPU kernel cost multipliers. Estimated cost is a heuristic (not billing).
- Telemetry signals to collect: token_count, input_tokens, output_tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_type, model_variant, queue_depth, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size, grpc_retry_count.
- Security: test artifacts must not contain customer prompt text. The harness should hash any raw prompt text with SHA256 and strip PII prior to upload.

Sample CI job (redwood-ci.yml snippet)

jobs:
  consumption-test:
    runs-on: runner-staging
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        run: git checkout ${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Run consumption scenario S1
        run: >
          consumption-sim run --scenario S1 --model $MODEL_VARIANT --duration 20m --concurrency 16 --export s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/${{ github.sha }}/telemetry.json
      - name: Compare and evaluate
        run: >
          comparison-service compare --baseline s3://redwood-test-artifacts/baselines/S1/latest.json --candidate s3://redwood-test-artifacts/runs/${{ github.sha }}/telemetry.json --out /tmp/compare.json && 
          gating-rule-evaluator --artifact /tmp/compare.json || exit 1

Dependencies and integration points

- redwood-telemetry (ingestion pipeline) — required for dashboards and alerts.
- Release Orchestrator — must support webhook-based blocking on failed CI gating results.
- S3 test-artifacts bucket and telemetry-schema linting utility.
- Developer sandbox runtime and local-telemetry sink (eng-developer-experience collaboration).

Ownership and rollout plan

- Phase 0 (MVP, 4 weeks): implement consumption-sim core + S1 and S2 scenarios, telemetry exporter, basic comparison service, and CI template. Owner: Product + Eng-serving-runtime.
- Phase 1 (8 weeks): add S3 artifact retention, S3 baseline management UI, automation for canary blocking webhook, and S3-based result viewers. Owner: Eng-platform + Product.
- Phase 2 (12 weeks): implement all 6 scenarios, developer local runtime, fidelity comparator improvements (embed-sim), and integration with Optimize recommendations for kernel/quantization experiments. Owner: Applied ML + Optimize + Product.

Rollout criteria

- Must have 3 successful runs by distinct feature teams in staging with no gating failures for non-risky changes.
- CI job latency for a full run must be under 45 minutes for S1/S2 baseline runs.

Appendix: Example telemetry JSON schema (flattened fields)

- run_id: string
- scenario_id: string
- start_ts: ISO8601 string
- end_ts: ISO8601 string
- tokens_input: int
- tokens_output: int
- latency_p50_ms: float
- latency_p95_ms: float
- latency_p99_ms: float
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: float
- estimated_cost_usd: float
- model_variant: string
- kernel_profile: string
